scope: Model/editor semantic and pedagogy review of Lesson 0131; not an independent human or real-learner test.

englishNaturalness.evidence: ‘It takes an hour.’ and ‘The walk takes an hour too.’ are grammatical, natural duration statements; all English distractors are grammatical and natural alternatives.

persianMeaningQuality.evidence: Persian copy consistently maps hour to «ساعت» and preserves the sixty-minute time-unit meaning.

pedagogicalClarity.evidence: The learner first encounters the guided exchange, then listening recognition and a supported sentence reconstruction, and finally performs hidden-answer retrieval.

distractorQuality.evidence: A04 and A05 distractors contrast duration or intent without malformed English; each wrong English option has an explicit model audit and Persian contrast reason.

dialoguePlausibility.evidence: سارا و روبی در مسیر خانه زمان رفت‌وآمد با اتوبوس و پیاده را مقایسه می‌کنند.

difficultyFit.evidence: The target noun is concrete and frequent; the duration frame stays controlled while the familiar indefinite-article pattern an hour is explicitly recycled.

repetitionUsefulness.evidence: hour recurs across recognition, dialogue, listening, sentence reconstruction, transfer, and hidden retrieval.

transferQuality.evidence: The duration moves from the bus to walking while retaining the same time-unit sense.

overallCoherence.evidence: Outcome, construction, scenario, learner turns, grammar focus, supported reconstruction, and final retrieval all align to the duration objective.

learnerExperience.evidence: Dependency order is internally sound, but no real learner test is claimed; perceived pacing and ease remain unverified.

runtimeAssetGrounding.evidence: No visual is claimed. A03 uses audio-required T01/T02 after A02 exposes them; A06 sentence_order uses audio-required T02 and permits replay.

limitations: No independent human or real learner test has been performed.
Only the bounded sixty-minute noun sense of hour and familiar an-hour article pattern are reviewed.
Generated audio pronunciation/prosody is not evaluated at this text stage.
resolvedFindings: English grammar, accepted speech consistency, and all English distractors were checked.
Persian orthography and translation consistency were checked.
Reference key, part of speech, sense key, and provisional spec hash were cross-checked against the worker packet.
CEFRJ-GRAM-13 is used only with the attested an hour form.
Learner-context dependency order was checked: dialogue exposure precedes A03 and A06 audio-dependent work; final retrieval references already exposed T04.
No unsupported visual claim exists and every listening source is an audio-required turn.
Sentence reconstruction is practice-only, hides the completed answer, uses exact T02 audio, and allows replay.
Final retrieval keeps the answer hidden before attempt.
Walking-group story arc returns after 5 Lessons with the learner role switched.
